name: OpenAI Containers (Code Interpreter / Hosted Shell)

modes.label: Responses API container (Code Interpreter / Hosted Shell), per minute with 5-min minimum
modes.note: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (2026-09-29): "Containers | Hosted Shell and Code Interpreter | 1 GB $0.03, 4 GB $0.12, 16 GB $0.48, 64 GB $1.92 per 20-minute session per container." + "Eligible container sessions will be billed by the minute, with a 5-minute minimum per session." Changelog 2026-06-02: "The underlying per-minute rate will remain the same." => hour = 3 x 20-min price ($0.0015/$0.006/$0.024/$0.096 per minute). memory_limit enum "1g"|"4g"|"16g"|"64g", default "1g" (API ref containers/create; openai-python container_create_params.py). vCPU per tier NOT published for Responses containers; the Agents API hosted sandboxes at the same 'standard container rates' are 1 vCPU/1 GB, 2/4 GB, 4/16 GB (see mode agents-api-hosted) - inference only, so vcpu left null here. Runtime Debian 12, /mnt/data, no sudo, no TTY; Python 3.11, Node 22.16, Java 17, PHP 8.2, Ruby 3.1, Go 1.23 (tools-shell guide). "A container expires if it is not used for 20 minutes" (expires_after {anchor:last_active_at, minutes}; max undocumented). GA since Code Interpreter 2025-05-20 / Hosted Shell 2026-02-10. Code Interpreter regional processing US + EU (your-data guide). Model tokens billed separately.

modes.label: Agents API OpenAI-hosted sandbox (public beta), small/medium/large at container rates
modes.note: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/environments/openai-hosted (2026-09-29): container_size small 1 vCPU/1 GB, medium 2/4 GB (default), large 4/16 GB; "OpenAI-hosted sandboxes use standard container rates." Prices mapped to the 1g/4g/16g container rows. min_billed_seconds/granularity inferred from the container rate card's per-minute/5-min rule (not stated for Agents API). "Connected sandboxes receive keep-alives, including between turns. If activity and keep-alives stop for an hour, the sandbox can be deleted. This timeout isn't configurable." => likely billed for the session's whole life until deleted (unconfirmed). Network default enabled; restricted = 1-100 exact hosts. Hosted browser via environment.desktop.enabled (agents-api/tools/computer-use). "The Agents API currently supports data residency only in the United States and does not support Zero Data Retention (ZDR)." Public beta since 2026-09-10 (changelog). Covered in depth by the 'new' research agent.

modes.label: Codex Cloud task VM (bundled in ChatGPT seat; tokens/credits only)

sizes.name: Pro / Business / Enterprise / Edu task VM

modes.note: Not a programmable sandbox: no public API (API-key plan has "No cloud-based features"). VM table (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments, 2026-09-29): "Plus, Edu Plus | 2 | 8 GiB | 8 GiB"; "Pro, Business, Enterprise | 4 | 16 GiB | 32 GiB"; "Edu, Edu Pro | 4 | 16 GiB | 32 GiB"; "Larger VMs and custom specifications are available for Enterprise. Contact your OpenAI account team". No compute charge: rate cards say cloud tasks are charged on "the actual input, cached input, and output tokens consumed" (help 11481834 / 20001415); 1 credit ~= $0.04 (derived: 250 credits per 1M GPT-6 Astra input tokens vs $10.00 API). hour=null because compute is bundled and capped by unpublished 5-hour/weekly usage limits. "a task's saved VM state is recoverable for up to seven days"; published environments snapshot the prepared filesystem. Network: allowlist presets / unrestricted, HTTPS network-secret substitution, Tailscale VPN, OIDC (Enterprise by request). Unsupported: "Computer and browser use".

modes.label: ChatGPT agent mode / Work cloud browser (per message, credits)
modes.note: Consumer/enterprise feature, no API. Business/Enterprise credit rate card (help 11481834): "Agent mode | 1 message | 30 credits" (~$1.20/message at derived $0.04/credit). "Work uses its own browser, running on a separate computer in the cloud" (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/browser). Work Cloud: "tasks run in VM-backed sandboxes" on "shared, OpenAI-managed infrastructure" (enterprise/chatgpt-work-cloud-security). Machine size and per-plan quotas unpublished / help center unreachable 2026-09-29.

plans.name: API pay as you go
plans.note: Containers bill on top of model tokens. Code Interpreter tool: "100 RPM per org" (tools-code-interpreter usage table) - encoded as max_starts_per_min (it caps tool requests, not container creations; hosted shell limit unpublished). No published container concurrency cap or per-usage-tier limits (rate-limits guide silent). Container expires 20 min after last activity; each distinct container is its own session.

plans.name: ChatGPT Plus
plans.note: $20/month (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing). Shared 5-hour + weekly agentic allowance (e.g. GPT-6 Sol 15-160 local messages / 5 h; "Cloud tasks may use more of your allowance"); extra usage via purchased credits.

plans.name: ChatGPT Pro $100
plans.note: Pro plans $100 / $200 / $500 per month; "Pro plans currently have no five-hour limit" (weekly limits may apply). New Pro $200 sign-ups paused since 2026-09-10 (help 9793128).

plans.name: ChatGPT Business
plans.note: "$20 / user / month*" (2+ users, billed annually) or "$25 per user per month when billed monthly"; per-seat limits, then workspace credits. Codex-only usage-based seats need credits from first use.

plans.name: ChatGPT Enterprise/Edu
plans.note: Contact sales. Flexible (credit) pricing: "no fixed rate limits"; larger/custom Codex Cloud VMs by request.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-29). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Code executions per container session
knobs.why: Calls that reuse one container (container_reference / auto-reuse within 20 min) are one session billed per minute with a 5-minute minimum. 200k isolated 1-minute runs on 1g cost $1,500 (5-min floor each) vs $300 if packed.

knobs.label: Idle tail until 20-min expiry is billed (x session hours)
knobs.why: OpenAI does not say whether the minutes between last use and expiry (20 min for containers, 1 h keep-alive window for Agents API sandboxes) are billed. If they are and you don't DELETE the container, factor = (session + tail)/session, e.g. 5-min run + 20-min tail = 5x. Default 1 assumes explicit deletion.

caveats: Model input/output tokens are billed separately and are not in this estimate; for short runs they often exceed container cost.

vCPU per Responses container tier is not published; the engine matches container-session on RAM only. The Agents API beta mode publishes 1/2/4 vCPU for 1/4/16 GB at the same rates (suggestive, not confirmed for Responses containers). 64 GB tier vCPU unknown.

Per-minute billing with 5-minute minimum applies to 'eligible' sessions since 2026-06-02 ('eligible' undefined); 2026-03-31 to 2026-06-01 each session was billed in full 20-minute blocks; before that $0.03-$1.92 per container.
Whether idle minutes until the 20-minute expiry are billed is undocumented; delete containers explicitly (DELETE /v1/containers/{id}). See knob idle_expiry_tail.

No snapshots or persistence: an expired container's data is 'discarded â€¦ not recoverable'. No documented max lifetime; keeping a container alive requires touching it at least every 20 minutes (or a larger expires_after.minutes, max undocumented).

Outbound network is disabled by default; enabling requires an admin-configured org allow list plus a per-request network_policy allowlist. domain_secrets inject credentials via a sidecar. No inbound ports/URLs.
Only rate limit published: Code Interpreter '100 RPM per org'. No container concurrency cap, no usage-tier table, nothing for hosted shell.
Disk size of containers not published ('ephemeral block storage').
Isolation: documented only as 'a fully sandboxed virtual machine'; hypervisor (gVisor/Firecracker/etc.) not named.
EU/US regional processing documented for the Code Interpreter tool; hosted shell not listed separately; whether the 10% data-residency uplift applies to containers is unknown.
Agents API hosted sandbox (beta mode): US-only data residency, no ZDR, 1-hour non-configurable keep-alive expiry; billing granularity inferred from the container rate card.

Codex Cloud and ChatGPT agent mode (alt modes) have no compute price: compute is bundled into ChatGPT seats and consumed as token credits (~$0.04/credit derived) under unpublished 5-hour/weekly limits; no public API, so not a substitute for a programmable sandbox.
Assistants API code interpreter ($0.03/session, 1-hour session) shut down 2026-08-26; not modelled.
soc2/hipaa/sso left null: not re-verified in this pass (previous card had soc2 true).

snapshot_auto.quote: A container expires if it is not used for 20 minutes. When this happens, using the container in `v1/responses` will fail. You'll still be able to see a snapshot of the container's metadata at its expiry, but all data associated with the container will be discarded from our systems and not recoverable.
snapshot_auto.note: Only metadata is kept at expiry; files and memory are discarded. Agents API hosted sandboxes are likewise deleted after 1 h without activity; only files in /workspace/outputs survive, as immutable artifacts published at the end of each turn (not a machine snapshot).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can't move a container from an expired state to an active one. Instead, create a new container and upload files again. Note that any state in the old container's memory (like python objects) will be lost.
snapshot_on_demand.note: The Containers API has create/list/retrieve/delete plus file endpoints only; no snapshot/checkpoint endpoint. Agents API 'environment_template_id' saves configuration only: 'Templates save configuration, not a running workspace.' Agents SDK snapshots apply to sandboxes you run elsewhere (local/E2B/Modal/...), not OpenAI containers.

harness_api.quote: The Agents API gives your application access to the Codex harness through an OpenAI-managed API.
harness_api.note: Agents API (public beta, OpenAI-Beta: agents=v1): POST /v1/agents/sessions with environment.type openai_hosted; stream events, webhooks, follow-up messages that steer an active turn ('A message sent during an active turn steers that turn'), list/retrieve/delete sessions. Harness = managed Codex only. Caveat: the harness runs on OpenAI's side and executes commands in the sandbox ('The harness runs commands in the sandbox directly'), rather than running inside it. The Responses API shell/code-interpreter tools alone would not count.

egress_allowlist.quote: Hosted containers don't have outbound network access by default. To enable it: 1. An admin must configure your org allow list in the dashboard. 2. You must explicitly set `network_policy` on the container environment in your request.
egress_allowlist.note: Default-deny. Containers API network_policy: 'disabled' or 'allowlist' with allowed_domains; org allow list caps request-level lists. Agents API hosted sandbox: network.access enabled (default) / disabled / restricted ('Restricted mode accepts 1-100 exact host names ... Do not include wildcards, protocols, paths, or ports'). No IP/CIDR rules documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: Restricted mode accepts 1–100 exact host names, such as `api.example.com`. Do not include wildcards, protocols, paths, or ports.
egress_http_rules.note: Allowlist is exact hostnames only; no method/path/header rules documented. The secret proxy does header substitution only (placeholder -> secret) for approved hosts.

ingress_rules.quote: Body Parameters: name, expires_after, file_ids, memory_limit, network_policy, skills
ingress_rules.note: No inbound access at all: no port exposure, preview URL or public IP in the Containers API, hosted shell or Agents API hosted sandbox; interaction is only via the API (files endpoints, tool calls). Nothing to control, so false (not applicable).

guest_firewall.quote: Hosted shell commands don't run with `sudo`.
guest_firewall.note: Documented as 'a fully sandboxed virtual machine' but commands run without root/sudo, so nftables/iptables cannot be configured. Hypervisor not named.

secret_proxy.quote: The model and runtime see placeholder names (for example, `$API_KEY`) instead of raw credentials. The auth-translation sidecar applies raw secret values only for approved destinations. Raw secret values don't persist on API servers and don't appear in model-visible context.
secret_proxy.note: Responses API containers: network_policy.domain_secrets [{domain,name,value}] for any allowlisted domain. Agents API hosted sandbox: vault credentials of type environment_variable with auth.networking.allowed_hosts; 'The sandbox receives a placeholder in the named environment variable. The real secret stays outside the sandbox.' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools/vaults). HTTPS only: 'The proxy supplies secrets only to HTTPS destinations on port 443 or 8443'; placeholder must be passed unchanged in a request header, cannot be used for signing. No database/SSH/git-over-SSH coverage.

volume_attach.quote: Hosted containers used by Hosted Shell and Code Interpreter may write temporary application state to the container filesystem (backed by ephemeral block storage) while the container is active. Container data is deleted when the container expires or is explicitly deleted.
volume_attach.note: Only ephemeral block storage; inputs via file_ids / inline files / skills copied in. No volume or mount parameter in the Containers API or Agents API hosted environment.

volume_shared.quote: Each session has a separate workspace. Files persist across turns while its sandbox exists.
volume_shared.note: No shared filesystem between containers/sessions; files must be copied in per container (file_ids).
